classification.difficultyReason: Apply the indicated reflection method with new bounds and adapt the inverse exponential and rectangle width for the factor 2.

content.prompt: Use a similar idea to find these integrals:

spec.description: Logarithmic curve with arrowheads, integer ticks −1 and 1–6 on both axes, and the region from x=1 to x=5 shaded green. No grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied curve and shaded region only; integral value is hidden.

answer.worked:
Reflect the shaded region across $y=x$. The reflected region lies between the $y$-axis and $y=e^x$, from $y=1$ to $y=5$. Subtract the area under the exponential curve from the bounding rectangle.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{rectangle}}&=5\ln 5\\A_{\text{under exponential}}&=\int_0^{\ln 5}e^x\,dx\\A_{\text{under exponential}}&=[e^x]_0^{\ln 5}\\A_{\text{under exponential}}&=5-1=4\\\int_1^5\ln x\,dx&=5\ln 5-4\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Vertically dilated logarithmic curve with arrowheads, integer ticks −1 and 1–6 on both axes, and the region from x=1 to x=3 shaded green. No grid.
spec.mathematics: y=2 ln x; shaded region 1≤x≤3, 0≤y≤2 ln x.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied curve and shaded region only; integral value is hidden.

answer.worked:
Reflect across $y=x$. The reflected curve is $x=2\ln y$, or $y=e^{x/2}$. The bounding rectangle has width $2\ln 3$ and height $3$.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{rectangle}}&=3(2\ln 3)=6\ln 3\\A_{\text{under exponential}}&=\int_0^{2\ln 3}e^{x/2}\,dx\\A_{\text{under exponential}}&=[2e^{x/2}]_0^{2\ln 3}\\A_{\text{under exponential}}&=2(3)-2(1)\\A_{\text{under exponential}}&=4\\\int_1^3 2\ln x\,dx&=6\ln 3-4\end{align*}$$
